subject: Civil Engineering
title: Evapotranspiration
description: A quick, practical guide to Evapotranspiration.

hook.text: A single oak tree pumps 40,000 gallons of water from the ground to the air each year.

buildup.text: Evapotranspiration combines evaporation from surfaces and transpiration from plants.

discovery.text: It's the largest water loss in most catchments — often 60% or more of all rainfall.

twist.text: Clearing forests reduces transpiration but increases runoff and erosion — a trade-off.

climax.text: The Penman-Monteith equation estimates ET from weather data — a UNESCO standard.

punchline.text: Most rain never reaches a river. Plants drink it first.

quiz.question: What does evapotranspiration include?
options: Only the evaporation from rivers, lakes, and oceans
Both evaporation from surfaces and water transpired by plants
Only the water absorbed by plant roots for growth
